label: final copy step of length-3 sequences (outputting orig token 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at step t=5 of L=3 sequences: the last step, where the model has fed back orig(1) and outputs the third original token (prev2_tok is <DEL>). It fires on about 93% of such steps and these hold about 92% of activation mass. Weaker activity occurs at the step before it in L=3 (recall_idx 1, t=4), and at recall_idx 2 in L=4 sequences (t=6), with roughly 0.05-0.15 of max. A trace appears at the last step of L=9 sequences. It never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter. Strongest activations come when the fed-back input is g, p, u or 3. Some of the misses (false positives) are sequences with repeated tokens, e.g. m m m.

issues: Small inaccuracy: the explanation says repeated-token sequences (e.g. m m m) are a false-positive class. In fact the predicate restricted to out_count>=2 has precision 0.91, about the same as overall, so repeated tokens are not a real false-positive source. The false positives on test look scattered. Several end in out_tok '0', but that subset still has precision 0.78 with n=64, so it is not systematic.

Recall is only 0.72 because of many weak activations: about 590 at L=4 recall_idx 2 and about 215 at L=3 recall_idx 1. They hold under 8% of the activation mass. Neither group can be predicted on its own: L=4/recall2 has P 0.04 and L=3/recall1 has P 0.08. Adding the L=4 subset with in_tok g/p/u lowers F1, from 0.813 to 0.75-0.80. The explanation already calls these weak secondary activations, so they are not a counterexample class.
Phrasing: 'fires on about 93% of those steps' is precision. It is correct, but it reads like a firing rate within the condition.

Checks that held up: never active in the original phase or on the delimiter; 91.6% of activation mass at t=5; 93.2% of mass at L=3; a trace at the last step of L=9 (69 steps, 0.7% of mass); top activations have the fed-back input p/3/g/u; test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.929, R 0.723, F1 0.813, mass recall 0.917).
